After graduating from the University of Wales, Dr. N. R. C. Birkett worked at the University of Loughborough teaching Mathematics to undergraduate engineering students. From here he moved to the University of Reading where he obtained his Ph.D. in 1986. Since then he has been a research fellow in the Mathematics Department at Reading, working on the application of numerical methods to the solution of engineering problems. These include the optimization of tidal power plants and silicon device process modelling. He is currently engaged in the development of 3-D finite element techniques for modelling the unsteady hydrodynamic flows associated with discharges in the marine environment

Ajith Amerasekera:  received his PhD from Loughborough University in England in 1986, for research into failure mechanisms in MOS devices. He spent one and a half years as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow working on breakdown mechanisms in SiO2. In 1988 he joined the I.C. Technology Division of Philips Research Labs, Eindhoven, The Netherlands, working on transistor reliability issues in advanced CMOS processes. His work focussed on the characterisation and development of ESD protection circuits and the analysis of process-related problems in this area. In 1991 he joined the Semiconductor Process and Design Center at Texas Instruments in Dallas. He is in the Device Design Group, working on ESD issues in design and modelling, for submicron and sub half-micron CMOS and BiCMOS technologies. His areas of interest include device modelling, high current effects, amorphous silicon breakdown and hot carriers. He has published a book and several papers on these subjects

Après une carrière entre la Suisse et l’Australie, Camille Moret est actuellement l’archiviste principale de l’Université de Loughborough (Angleterre). Titulaire d’un double master en Histoire et Esthétique du cinéma (MA), puis en Archives and Records Management (MLitt), elle se spécialise dans les images, leur médiation et leur réception lors de la mise en accès ; ainsi que dans la gestion de collections documentaires dite sensibles, donc l’interaction avec les publics et sujets-données vulnérables. Elle est membre professionnel de l’Australian Society of Archivists (ASAPR) et son travail lors des campagnes de numérisation des collections patrimoniales de la télévision publique australienne (SBS) a été encensé par le Prix de l’excellence en préservation des médias par la FIAF. Elle enseigne également le traitement documentaire des images en 71e section à l’université de Lille (GERIICO)
